0.long_answer: The benign adrenal tumor described is an adrenal adenoma, also known as an adrenocortical adenoma. It is a common incidental finding at autopsy, present in up to 10% of individuals. These tumors arise from the adrenal cortex and, while most are non-functioning, a subset can produce aldosterone. When such an adenoma secretes excess aldosterone, it leads to primary hyperaldosteronism, commonly known as Conn's syndrome. This condition is characterized by hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis, and it is often effectively treated by surgically removing the aldosterone-producing tumor.
